summary: From Whence Doth the Business Cometh? This week we look at the principal charterers for clean cargoes for Aframax, Panamax and Handymax tankers. Excluding failed fixtures, the Poten Spot Fixture Database records 3,271 fixtures in 2004.

children.summary: Aframax - Small in Number, Big in Size Forty-five charterers fixed spot voyages of clean trading Aframax tankers of which the top 17, or 38%, accounted for 80% of the business. The top five charterers concluded half of the charters.

children.title: Cargill
children.summary: Panamax - Small in Number and Not Quite so Big in Size A total of 53 charterers fixed Panamaxes for clean trading of which the top 9 accounted for 50% of fixtures with known charterers. The top 20, or 37%, accounted for 80% of all fixtures with known charterers.

children.title: Chevron Texaco
children.summary: Handymaxes - Large in Number and Dominating the Market A total of 113 charterers fixed Handymaxes for clean trading of which the top 9 charterers accounted for 50% of fixtures with known charterers and the top 27, or 24%, accounted for 80% of all fixtures. Shell, BP, and Chevron Texaco were the most active.

children.title: Only a Few Count
children.summary: The Pareto effect or 80/20 rule, where most of the activity in an industry is conducted by relatively few companies, holds in fixing tankers. In dirty cargoes, major oil companies dominate the few; but not in clean cargoes where oil traders join ranks with Big Oil to be counted among the few.
